clue.text: Architectural feature is half obscured by stucco

indicators.note: something obscured by a covering is hidden inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: stucco is a fine plaster for coating walls

indicators.note: only half of a two-letter word survives, the opening one

parts.note: the first half of the word is

explanation.surface: Part of a building's ornament has been half covered over by plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter from 'is' goes after the P of PLASTER, giving PILASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall, a classic piece of architectural decoration.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: resembling Mr Punch, Judy's husband in the puppet show

explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show; adding -Y to Punch makes a whimsical adjective, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy describes writing or speech with vigour and impact, and jokingly also means Punch-like.

clue.text: Herb has lots of varieties and grows easily at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each word in the run before it

parts.words: lots of varieties and grows easily
parts.note: initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A garden herb that comes in many kinds and is easy to cultivate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovage is a tall perennial plant of the celery family whose leaves are used as a culinary herb.

definitions.note: adjective standing for a cured sausage

parts.note: short for Sally, a stock crossword girl
French for friend or boyfriend

explanation.surface: A girl's French boyfriend has recovered from his illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cured' seems to mean healed in the surface; it is the meat-preserving sense, and the 's is just 'has' or a possessive glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a sausage preserved by salting and air-drying, i.e. a cured meat.

clue.text: Simple setter struggling to achieve state of financial security

parts.note: simple means easy

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter finds it hard work becoming well off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort without money worries.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A savage animal is losing its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or diminish in intensity, as a storm does when it weakens.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: resembling the comedian Russell Brand, a jokey adjective

explanation.walkthrough: Russell Brand is a British comedian known for showing off, so 'Brand-ish' is a playful description, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to flourish or wave something to display it, which is a form of showing off.

clue.text: Harry, Etta and Kath forming a pop group

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and worry, so the following letters are pushed around into a new order

parts.note: the two names taken as written, 'and' joining them

explanation.surface: Three friends, Harry, Etta and Kath, get together to start a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the third band member's name; it is the verb meaning harass, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Take That are a hugely successful British boy band formed in Manchester in 1990.

parts.note: fine means super, excellent
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: The religious reformer's opponent is a decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Luther' summons Martin Luther, but it is Lex Luthor, the comic-book villain, with the spelling bent for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman is the comic-book hero whose arch-nemesis is the villain Lex Luthor.

clue.text: Herzog, for example, is German writer

parts.note: Herzog is a novel by Saul Bellow
the German word for is

explanation.surface: Herzog, say, is a German author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herzog' suggests the German film-maker Werner Herzog; here it is Saul Bellow's 1964 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is an author of novels, a kind of writer.

clue.text: Support for king in Lancashire town

indicators.note: in tells us one item is placed within the other

parts.note: Bacup is a small town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Backing for a monarch found in a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Backup is reserve help or support held ready in case it is needed.

parts.note: high as in high-ranking or high-priority
mass as in mass-market, appealing to many

explanation.surface: A significant church service that is well attended.
explanation.definitionFit: High Mass is a full ceremonial Eucharist with music and incense, a church service.

indicators.note: dissolute means debauched, loose-living, so the following letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A worn-out, debauched old hack from Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the journalist in charge of a newspaper's content, a senior newspaper professional.

parts.note: a shop that keeps an item in store stocks it
to husband land is an old sense meaning to farm or cultivate it, i.e. till it

explanation.surface: Someone holds their husband so that he cannot move at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a spouse; it is the verb meaning cultivate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means utterly without movement, as still as a post.

parts.note: a bra is an item of supporting underwear

indicators.note: trashing means wrecking, so the following letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A fan vandalising the Latvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latvia's capital' looks like it will be Riga; Latvia's letters are only fodder and the city is elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia, on the Danube.

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
a break is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: A first delivery in a game that spun after bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an off break is a delivery from a spin bowler that turns on pitching; the surface uses 'turned' and 'opening' in that cricketing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An off break is a type of spinning delivery bowled in cricket, so it is a ball in that sport's jargon.

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the preceding letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Detain a lawbreaker in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' is the obvious definition, but its letters are needed as fodder; 'jail', used as a verb, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to hold them back from freedom, which is to restrain them.

clue.text: Plant is strangely shaped with no end of appeal

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
no, as in nil, is the zero-shaped letter O

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: last letter of appeal

explanation.surface: A plant has an odd form and nothing attractive about it.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces go into the mix together; 'no' supplies the O and 'end of appeal' the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-family flower, in Greek myth said to cover the Elysian fields.

clue.text: It costs nothing to talk right

parts.note: something that costs nothing is free
speech is the act of talking

explanation.surface: Talking is free, and it is correct to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as an adverb, correct; it is the noun, an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Free speech is a basic civil liberty, a right guaranteed in many constitutions.

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means sitting below it, so the earlier-named piece comes second in the answer

parts.note: a palm is a tree
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A golfer hesitates after his ball lands beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' puts the second piece below, i.e. after, the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Palmer was a celebrated American professional golfer, winner of seven major championships.

clue.text: Fake doctor dupes others to start with

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the following letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to start with takes just the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: first letter of others

explanation.surface: A bogus medic first fools other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun paired with 'Fake'; it is the verb, tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or not genuine, pretending to be something it is not.

parts.note: standard abbreviation for English
Ernie Els, the South African golfer

explanation.surface: An English golfer who changed the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx, a famous revolutionary thinker.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
prickly in the sense of causing a tingling itch

explanation.surface: A single man is touchy and mean-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Bachelor stands for 'is' in the surface and is ignored in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy is an informal word for malicious or catty in remarks about others.

clue.text: He murders Jack and Jenny at home

parts.note: a jack is a male donkey or ass
a jenny is a female donkey or ass
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A killer strikes at Jack and Jenny in their house.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Jenny look like two victims; they are a male and female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer, especially one who murders a prominent person, so he is one who murders.

parts.note: a Cockney drops his aitches, saying 'e for he
to land a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A Londoner gets hold of some antelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Cockney catches' as 'he lands' in a Cockney accent: 'e lands. Cockneys are working-class East Londoners famed for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes with spiralled horns.

clue.text: Bird finally caught by extremely intelligent rodent

indicators.note: finally keeps only the last letter of the word beside it

parts.note: last letter of caught

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of intelligent
a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A bird is eventually caught by a very clever rat or mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here means next to, so the pieces sit side by side rather than one inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is the old full name for the tit, a small songbird; it is a bird, not a mouse.

indicators.note: an explosive blast scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bomb wired up to set a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to set alight, so it means to fire in the sense of igniting.

clue.text: Beautiful girl, mad with love, quietly leaves work

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: an opus is a musical or literary work
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A lovely girl, crazy with passion, slips silently out of the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorious means magnificent or splendid, a strong synonym for beautiful.
